analysis.title: ZipRecruiter Inc. (ZIP) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Marketplace Improvements Drive Accelerating Growth
key_insights: ZIP Q3'26 revenue of $124mm and Adj. EBITDA of $21mm both beat GS, consensus and company guidance (revenue guide $118-124mm, Adj. EBITDA guide $13-19mm).
Management raised FY26 guidance to +4-5% YoY revenue growth (from +LSD% previously) and Adj. EBITDA margin of 13-14% (from 12-14%). FY25 Adj. EBITDA margin was 9%.

Product improvements drove qualified applications +49% QoQ and employer response rates per application roughly 3x YoY. Quarterly Paid Employers rose +10% YoY to 73.9K, with strength across new employers, reactivations and retention.
Be Seen First is used by 9% of applicants, and those users are 2.5x more likely to receive an employer message. A new follow-up feature drove more than 4.5x more message exchanges.
Traffic from AI platforms nearly doubled YoY. Management describes these users as a fast-growing, high-converting source of job seekers.
Performance-based revenue grew +13% YoY and is now 25% of total revenue. Enterprise adoption of automated campaign performance solutions grew +23% YoY.
Revenue per Paid Employer fell 2% YoY to $1,683, mainly because new Quarterly Paid Employers contributed revenue for only part of the quarter.
Q4'26 Adj. EBITDA guidance implies slight YoY margin contraction because of continued sales and marketing investment to sustain topline momentum.
Labor market backdrop: total hires and quits are stable sequentially but near their lowest levels since 2015, with limited visibility on the timing of a recovery.

GS keeps its Neutral rating and raises its 12-month price target to $5.50 from $5.00, which is 28.2% upside from the $4.29 price. The target blends 1.0x EV/Sales (from 0.85x) on NTM+1 estimates with a 7.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA multiple on NTM+4 estimates discounted back 3 years at 12%.

GS raised estimates. 2026E revenue is $470mm (from $460mm) and 2027E revenue is $516mm (from $493mm). 2027E GAAP EPS is $0.07 (from $0.02). Q4'26E revenue is $120mm (from $114mm) while Q4'26E Adj. EBITDA is cut to $18mm (from $20mm).
GS scenario analysis gives a $2.50 downside value (-45%), a $5.50 base value and an $8.50 upside value.

market_movers.rationale: GS maintained Neutral and raised the PT from $5.00 to $5.50 after a Q3'26 beat and a raised FY26 outlook. The higher target reflects a higher EV/Sales multiple of 1.0x (from 0.85x), applied to higher estimates.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported (7/10 print, reported 11/9-11/10): revenue $124mm vs GS est $121mm and consensus $121mm, guidance $118-124mm. Beat of 3% vs both.
Q3'26 reported Adj. EBITDA $21mm vs GS est $16mm and consensus $16mm, guidance $13-19mm. Adj. EBITDA margin 16.7% vs GS est 13.4% and consensus 13.3%.
Q3'26 reported GAAP EPS $0.06 vs GS est $(0.04) and consensus $(0.01).
Q3'26 reported Quarterly Paid Employers 73.9K vs GS est 70.3K. Reported Revenue per Paid Employer $1,683 vs GS est $1,717 (-2%). Reported GAAP gross margin 89.8% vs consensus 89.8%.
GS Q4'26 estimates (new, vs prior): revenue $120mm (from $114mm), Adj. EBITDA $18mm (from $20mm), GAAP EPS $(0.00) (from $0.01).

GS FY26E estimates (new, vs prior): revenue $470mm (from $460mm), Adj. EBITDA $63mm (from $60mm), GAAP EPS $0.48 (from $0.41). GS FY27E: revenue $516mm (from $493mm), Adj. EBITDA $77mm (from $75mm), GAAP EPS $0.07 (from $0.02). GS FY28E: revenue $561mm (from $536mm), Adj. EBITDA $93mm, GAAP EPS $0.23 (from $0.18).
Company guidance (raised): FY26 revenue growth +4-5% YoY and Adj. EBITDA margin 13-14%, versus a flat revenue outlook entering the year and 9% Adj. EBITDA margin in FY25.
risk_factors: Job openings and employer demand could come in above or below GS estimates and change revenue growth.
Competitive intensity from Indeed, Glassdoor, CareerBuilder and Monster could differ from GS estimates.
Marketing spend could differ from GS modeling assumptions.
Sustained improvement or decline in hiring.
Labor market uncertainty persists, with hires and quits near their lowest levels since 2015 and limited visibility on a recovery.

tension_points.bull_case: Product improvements lifted qualified applications +49% QoQ, employer response rates ~3x YoY and Quarterly Paid Employers +10% YoY. Management raised FY26 revenue growth to +4-5% and Adj. EBITDA margin to 13-14%.
tension_points.bear_case: Hires and quits remain near their lowest levels since 2015 with limited visibility on recovery. Revenue per Paid Employer fell 2% YoY, and Q4'26 Adj. EBITDA guidance implies slight margin contraction on higher sales and marketing spend.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS names a decline in job openings or employer demand below GS estimates, or a sustained decline in hiring, as key risks to revenue growth.
